title: Utv library use cases
description: What an application developer does with the C# library, step by step: mostly through the typed API in Typed/, which calls the JSON layer in this folder.

entities.name: Create a date
entities.description: A developer makes a calendar date from its fields or from text, and learns why it cannot exist when it can't (tasks a-date and feb-30).
entities.goal: Hold a value that names a real day, such as 5 November 2026, or know exactly why the fields or text name none.
preconditions: The application references the Utv package and imports namespace Utv.
postconditions: The developer holds an immutable CivilDate, or an Invalid or Unsupported outcome whose diagnostic code says why there is none.
Nothing was read from the host: no clock, zone or culture.

flow.action: Calls CivilDate.Of(year, month, day), CivilDate.TryOf(year, month, day) or CivilDate.Parse(text).
Writes the fields as a UTV civil date (or reads the text with the text-form grammar) and checks it structurally.
Checks the month and that the day exists in that month of the proleptic Gregorian calendar, with the year as a BigInteger.
Returns the CivilDate (Of), or Outcome<CivilDate>.Unique (TryOf, Parse). Its ToString() is the text form, 2026-11-05; years beyond 9999 and before 1 are ordinary dates (+275760-09-13, -0500-03-01).

alternatives.condition: The day does not exist in the month, such as 30 February 2026 or 29 February 1900.
alternatives.outcome: TryOf and Parse return Invalid with day-out-of-range; Of throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException for parameter day.

alternatives.condition: The month is outside 1..12, such as 13.
alternatives.outcome: Invalid with month-out-of-range; Of throws ArgumentOutOfRangeException for parameter month.

alternatives.condition: The text is not in the grammar.
alternatives.outcome: Parse returns Invalid with syntax.

alternatives.condition: The text is valid ISO 8601 outside this profile: a week date (2026-W45-4), an ordinal date (2026-309) or basic format (20261105).
alternatives.outcome: Parse returns Unsupported with unsupported-form.

alternatives.condition: The text is a valid value of another kind or form, such as a date-time.
alternatives.outcome: CivilDate.Parse returns Invalid with kind-mismatch.

entities.name: Add months
entities.description: A developer adds months (or years) to a date and finds out when the day is missing from the target month (task month-end).
entities.goal: Get the date one or more months later, and decide what to do when that month has no such day.
preconditions: The developer holds a CivilDate (or a CivilDateTime or ZonedIntent, which have the same AddMonths).
postconditions: The developer holds the later date, or an Outcome<CivilDate>.None whose diagnostic month-end names the missing day.
A date was clamped only if the developer passed MonthEnd.Constrain.

flow.action: Calls date.AddMonths(n) (or AddYears(n), or Add(Period.Months(n))).
Adds 12·years + months to the year and month with the JSON layer's add.
Checks that the day exists in the resulting month.
Returns Outcome<CivilDate>.Unique with the later date.

alternatives.condition: The day is missing from the target month, as for 31 January 2026 plus one month.
alternatives.outcome: Outcome<CivilDate>.None with a month-end warning, 2026-02 has no day 31. The developer may ask again with date.AddMonths(n, MonthEnd.Constrain), which returns 28 February 2026 as a plain CivilDate.

alternatives.condition: The developer passes MonthEnd.Reject to the overload that takes a policy.
alternatives.outcome: ArgumentException: that overload always answers, so it takes only MonthEnd.Constrain.

alternatives.condition: The period given to CivilDate.Add has hours, minutes or seconds.
alternatives.outcome: Outcome<CivilDate>.Invalid with kind-mismatch: a date does not take time components.

entities.name: Resolve a zoned time
entities.description: A developer turns a wall time in an IANA zone into an instant, and sees it elsewhere, with DST gaps and overlaps reported rather than guessed (tasks meeting-in-paris, dst-gap and dst-overlap).
entities.goal: Find the instant a meeting at 09:00 in Paris happens, and what the clock in New York says then.
preconditions: The developer has a zone-rule bundle in the format of conformance/rules/demo-zones.json that covers the date.
postconditions: The developer holds the instant, or knows the wall time happens never or twice, or that the rules cannot say.
The ZonedIntent still holds the wall time and zone as written: resolving does not change it.

flow.action: Loads the rules with ZoneRules.Load(path) and holds them in TemporalContext.With(rules).
Makes the wall time a zoned intention: CivilDateTime.Of(2027, 6, 1, 9, 0).InZone("Europe/Paris").
Calls zoned.Resolve(ctx), optionally with a Gap, an Overlap or a ResolutionPolicy.
Checks that the zone is in the rules and that the wall time lies at least a day inside their validity window.
Finds the candidate instants: for each offset in force within a day, the wall time minus that offset, kept when the zone's offset at that instant is that offset.
Returns Outcome<Instant>.Unique for exactly one candidate.
Calls instant.InZone("America/New_York", ctx) and reads the wall time there, 03:00, with the offset in force asserted.

alternatives.condition: The file is not a well-formed rule bundle.
alternatives.outcome: ZoneRules.Load throws FormatException.

alternatives.condition: The zone id is empty or is not an IANA zone name.
alternatives.outcome: InZone throws ArgumentException.

alternatives.condition: The zone is not in the rules.
alternatives.outcome: Outcome<Instant>.Unsupported with unknown-zone; the message lists the zones the rules have.

alternatives.condition: The wall time is less than a day inside the rules' validity window, or outside it.
alternatives.outcome: Outcome<Instant>.Unsupported with outside-rule-window: the rules are never extrapolated.

alternatives.condition: The policy names a gap or overlap rule the library does not implement (built from GapPolicy or OverlapPolicy).
alternatives.outcome: Outcome<Instant>.Unsupported with unsupported-policy.

alternatives.condition: The ZonedIntent asserts an offset that no candidate has (including any asserted offset in a gap).
alternatives.outcome: Outcome<Instant>.Invalid with offset-mismatch.

alternatives.condition: No candidate: the wall time falls in a gap, such as 02:30 on 8 March 2026 in New York, and the policy is the default (Strict) or Gap.PreserveUnresolved.
alternatives.outcome: Outcome<Instant>.None with a gap warning naming the transition, clocks jump from 02:00 to 03:00 in America/New_York.

alternatives.condition: No candidate, and the developer passed Gap.ShiftForward.
alternatives.outcome: Outcome<Instant>.Unique: the wall time minus the offset before the gap, which is the instant labelled 03:30 EDT.

alternatives.condition: Two candidates: the wall time falls in an overlap, such as 01:30 on 1 November 2026 in New York, and the policy is the default (Strict).
alternatives.outcome: Outcome<Instant>.Multiple with both instants, ascending, and an ambiguous warning (clocks go back from 02:00 to 01:00). Overlap.All gives the same without the warning.

alternatives.condition: Two candidates, and the developer passed Overlap.Earliest or Overlap.Latest.
alternatives.outcome: Outcome<Instant>.Unique with the earlier or the later instant.

alternatives.condition: The other zone is not in the rules, or the instant is outside their window.
alternatives.outcome: Outcome<ZonedIntent>.Unsupported with unknown-zone or outside-rule-window.

entities.name: Compare values
entities.description: A developer asks which of two values comes first: directly for dates and other values whose order needs no rules, and through a context for zoned values, where the answer may be several (task compare-dates).
entities.goal: Know whether one value comes before, with or after another, or that the order cannot be told.
preconditions: The developer holds two values of the same type; for zoned values, a TemporalContext with rules that cover them.
postconditions: The developer holds an order, or an outcome that lists every possible order, or says why there is none.

flow.action: Compares two dates with a < b (or CompareTo); the same works for year-months, times, date-times, fixed-offset date-times and instants.
Orders them with the JSON layer's compare: civil fields (a missing second counts as 0), POSIX seconds, or fixed-offset date-times as instants.
For two ZonedIntents, which have no comparison operators, calls ctx.Compare(a, b).
Resolves both with ResolutionPolicy.Strict and compares every pair of candidate instants.
Returns Outcome<Ordering>.Unique (Before, Equal or After) when every pair agrees.

alternatives.condition: The order depends on which side of a DST overlap is meant, as for 01:30 and 01:45 on 1 November 2026 in New York.
alternatives.outcome: Outcome<Ordering>.Multiple with the possible orderings and an ambiguous warning.

alternatives.condition: A side does not resolve: it falls in a gap, its zone is unknown, or it is outside the rules' window.
alternatives.outcome: That side's None or Unsupported outcome, with its diagnostics (gap, unknown-zone, outside-rule-window), as an Outcome<Ordering>.

alternatives.condition: Values held as JSON are compared with Calendar.Compare and one has a named zone.
alternatives.outcome: unsupported with needs-zone-rules: resolve them to instants first.

entities.name: Convert to and from .NET
entities.description: A developer brings a .NET date or time into UTV, such as a clock reading, and takes it back out (tasks now and round-trip).
entities.goal: Use UTV alongside .NET's own types without either side guessing what a value means.
preconditions: The developer has a .NET value: a DateTimeOffset read from the clock, a DateOnly, a DateTime or a TimeSpan.
postconditions: The developer holds the UTV value, or the .NET value back, or an outcome that says why it could not be converted.
The library never read the clock or the host's zone; the developer read the clock and passed the reading in.

flow.action: Reads the clock in their own code, for example DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.

Chooses the type that names the intent: Instant.FromDateTimeOffset for a moment, FixedOffsetDateTime.FromDateTimeOffset for a wall time at an offset, CivilDate.FromDateOnly, CivilDateTime.FromDateTime or Instant.FromDateTime.
Converts with Interop: ticks become an exact POSIX instant, or wall fields and an offset in seconds.
Converts back with ToDateTimeOffset(), ToDateOnly(), ToTimeOnly(), ToDateTime() or ToTimeSpan().
Checks that .NET can hold the value and returns Outcome<T>.Unique; a FixedOffsetDateTime that came from a DateTimeOffset gives back an EqualsExact copy.

alternatives.condition: A DateTime of Kind Local, as DateTime.Now returns.
alternatives.outcome: Unsupported with local-zone: the host's zone is never read.

alternatives.condition: A DateTime of Kind Utc given to CivilDateTime.FromDateTime, or of Kind Unspecified given to Instant.FromDateTime.
alternatives.outcome: Invalid with intent-required: the developer must say whether it is a moment or a wall time.

alternatives.condition: The value is outside what .NET holds: a year outside 1..9999 (CivilDate.Of(10000, 1, 1).ToDateOnly()), nanoseconds that are not a multiple of 100, an offset that is not whole minutes or beyond ±14:00.
alternatives.outcome: Unsupported with out-of-native-range.

alternatives.condition: An Instant is converted to DateTimeOffset.
alternatives.outcome: Unique at +00:00 with an info diagnostic offset-not-known: a UTV instant knows UTC, not a local offset.

alternatives.condition: Through the JSON layer, a zoned date-time with an asserted offset is converted to DateTimeOffset.
alternatives.outcome: NativeResult with IsLossy and a zone-dropped warning; without an asserted offset, unsupported with needs-zone-rules.

entities.name: Read and write text
entities.description: A developer reads ISO 8601 / RFC 9557 text or the UTV text form into values and writes values back as text (task parse-offsets, and every ToString).
entities.goal: Turn text from a log, a file or a user into a value without losing what the text says, and print values so that they read back the same.
preconditions: The developer has text, or a typed value to print.
postconditions: The developer holds the value the text denotes, of the type it denotes, or an outcome that says why there is none.
Printed text parses back to an equal value, or the value has no text form.

flow.action: Calls Temporal.Parse(text) for any value, or T.Parse(text) for one type, such as Instant.Parse.

Reads the text: brackets as an interval, P… as a period, a slash as an EDTF interval, anything else as an ISO 8601 / RFC 9557 point. Z and -00:00 give an instant; +00:00 gives a fixed-offset date-time; [Area/Location] gives a zoned intention.
Reads the UTV value into its typed value and returns Outcome<T>.Unique; Temporal.Parse returns an ITemporalValue to switch on.
Calls value.ToString().
Formats the value's JSON as text, parses it back and checks it is the same value, then returns the text.

alternatives.condition: The text is outside the grammar, or a field is out of range (2026-02-30, 25:00, +19:00).
alternatives.outcome: Invalid with syntax, day-out-of-range, field-out-of-range or offset-out-of-range.

alternatives.condition: Valid notation this profile does not handle: week, ordinal and basic-format dates, a decimal period component, an EDTF qualifier (1347~), an interval with no point.
alternatives.outcome: Unsupported with unsupported-form.

alternatives.condition: An annotation other than one [Area/Location], or a zone after Z; second 60; 24:00; more than nine fraction digits.
alternatives.outcome: Unsupported with unsupported-annotation, leap-second, end-of-day or implementation-limit.

alternatives.condition: An interval that ends before it starts, or whose ends are of different kinds.
alternatives.outcome: Invalid with reversed-interval or kind-mismatch.

alternatives.condition: The text is another kind of value than the type asked for, such as 2026-11-05T13:30:00Z given to FixedOffsetDateTime.Parse.
alternatives.outcome: Invalid with kind-mismatch.

alternatives.condition: The value has no text form: a period with mixed signs, or a POSIX or SI second count.
alternatives.outcome: A Period prints its UTV JSON instead; PosixSeconds and ElapsedSeconds print a display string such as 3600.75 s (POSIX), which does not parse.

entities.name: Validate UTV JSON
entities.description: A developer receives UTV JSON, checks it structurally and, for dates, semantically, and reads it into typed values.
entities.goal: Accept only UTV values this library understands, and tell a malformed value from a newer one and from an impossible date.
preconditions: The developer has JSON text that claims to be a UTV value.
postconditions: The developer holds a utv-result/1.0 result for the JSON and, when it is valid and of an everyday shape, a typed value.
Nothing that the library does not understand was accepted.

flow.action: Calls UtvValidator.ValidateStructural(json).
Parses the JSON strictly into its own tree.
Checks that schema is exactly utv/1.0, before anything else.
Checks the envelope's properties and every value, top-level and nested, against the embedded schema/utv-1.0.schema.json, and returns valid.
For a civil value, calls GregorianCivil.Validate(json), which repeats the structural check and then judges year, month and day.
Reads the value with T.FromJson(json), such as CivilDate.FromJson, or Temporal.FromJson(json) for any type.
Reads the value into its typed value, checks that ToJson of it gives back the same JSON, and returns Outcome<T>.Unique.

alternatives.condition: Malformed JSON: comments, trailing commas, NaN, trailing content, unpaired surrogates, nesting deeper than 128, or a key repeated at any depth.
alternatives.outcome: invalid with malformed-json or duplicate-key at the key's JSON Pointer.

alternatives.condition: A well-formed identifier other than utv/1.0, such as utv/2.0.
alternatives.outcome: unsupported with unsupported-version; a newer version's unknown kinds and properties are never called invalid.

alternatives.condition: A missing, non-string or malformed identifier, such as utv/4.
alternatives.outcome: invalid with unknown-schema.

alternatives.condition: An unknown top-level property, a kind outside the 26 core kinds, or any other schema violation.
alternatives.outcome: invalid with unknown-property, unknown-kind or the schema codes (missing-property, wrong-type, pattern-mismatch, schema-violation, …).

alternatives.condition: A well-formed civil value names a missing day, such as 29 February 2026, or a month outside 1..12.
alternatives.outcome: invalid with day-out-of-range or month-out-of-range.

alternatives.condition: Another calendar (a Hebrew date) or another kind.
alternatives.outcome: unsupported with unsupported-calendar or unsupported-kind.

alternatives.condition: The value is of another kind or form than the type asked for.
alternatives.outcome: Outcome<T>.Invalid with kind-mismatch.

alternatives.condition: A valid UTV value no typed type holds: a recurrence, a zoned date, a floating date-time with a resolutionPolicy, extra properties.
alternatives.outcome: Outcome<T>.Unsupported with unsupported-operand; the JSON layer still handles it.

alternatives.condition: FromJson is given JSON that is not structurally valid.
alternatives.outcome: Outcome<T>.Invalid with malformed-value followed by the structural codes.
